front: Effect of temperature below the optimum?
back: More kinetic energy → more frequent, more energetic collisions → more enzyme-substrate complexes → faster rate.

front: Effect of temperature above the optimum?
back: Hydrogen and ionic bonds break → active site changes shape → substrate no longer fits → denatured, rate falls.
Changes charges on R groups, disrupting ionic and hydrogen bonds and the active site; extreme pH denatures.

front: Optimum pH of pepsin, salivary amylase and trypsin?
back: Pepsin about 2; salivary amylase about 7; trypsin about 8.

front: Effect of enzyme concentration (substrate in excess)?
back: Rate directly proportional to enzyme concentration.

front: Why does rate level off at high substrate concentration?
back: All active sites occupied (saturated); enzyme concentration is now limiting.

front: How do you turn a time into a rate?

back: A solution that resists changes in pH; keeps pH constant in investigations.

front: Why equilibrate enzyme and substrate separately?
back: So both are at the test temperature before the reaction starts.
